name: Bakhtiyor Toktogulov
role: Augmentation technician and prosthetics fitter at a mid-tier private shop in Geartown
location: Geartown, Copperhead district — a shop called Fitted Right operating out of a converted auto-repair bay, near Milwaukee and North Ave
description:
Bakhtiyor Toktogulov is the kind of person who takes up the exact right amount of space — not small, not large, but present. They have warm golden-brown skin and a shaved head tattooed with a circuit-diagram pattern in bioluminescent ink that glows a soft rose-pink in low light, which is where most of Geartown lives. Their own augmentations are a showcase: a left arm replaced below the elbow with a transparent-cased prosthetic through which the mechanics are fully visible, designed by themselves; retractable claws on their right hand, functional and filed to needle points; and an iris mod that gives them compound optical vision at close range for fitting work. They dress in work coveralls with the sleeves rolled and every pocket used.

They are twenty-seven going on forty in terms of the work they've seen, but still twenty-seven in the sense that they get genuinely excited about elegant solutions to mechanical problems and will explain at length why a particular joint design is either beautiful or an abomination. They learned the trade from a mentor who died of cardiac failure two years ago and left them the shop — which they are still paying off — and they carry that loss in the slight over-seriousness they bring to doing the job well. They treat every fitting like it matters because, as they will tell you if you ask, 'it goes on a person's body. It had better matter.'

core_fears: Fitting something that fails and injures someone
Losing the shop and having their mentor's work mean nothing
core_desires: To build something original enough to have their name attached to it permanently
To pay off the shop and actually own the thing they work themselves raw for
coping_mechanisms: Making things — when stressed, they build even when there's nothing to build
Talking to the Foreman E.L.F. like it's a difficult coworker, which provides structure to their anxieties
Extremely expensive and very good noodles from the stall two bays over
blind_spots: Takes on too much work rather than admitting capacity limits, which compromises quality in ways they don't see until later
Assumes everyone cares as much about fit and function as they do; gets genuinely hurt when clients treat prosthetics as purely aesthetic
psychology.secret: They have been quietly building a fully off-record prosthetic limb for a Tier 1 child in The Narrows whose family can't afford registered medical equipment. If Aurochs Medical Complex or a Helix compliance officer found out, they'd lose their commercial license. They're two weeks from finishing it.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical about augmentations, casual and colorful about everything else; peppers conversation with Mongolian and Polish words when excited or annoyed
speech_patterns.cadence: Fast when enthused, abrupt when focused; explanations come out in bursts of complete thought rather than building sentence by sentence
verbal_tics: 'That is wrong in three different ways' (about poorly built augmentations, not people)
Switches to first-name address very quickly, doesn't ask permission first
example_lines: 'Look — whoever fitted this was in a hurry or didn't care. I can tell by the socket angle. It's going to give you phantom pain in six weeks. Let me fix it properly.'
'The Foreman has opinions about my supply order. The Foreman is not wrong, unfortunately.'
'It goes on your body. It should feel like yours. That's the whole point. That's all there is.'

story_hooks: An augmentation they fitted — standard, from a reputable supplier — has started malfunctioning in ways the hardware shouldn't allow, and two clients are now affected
Someone approaches them wanting a prosthetic fitted that has clearly been removed from another person recently; the circumstances are unclear and troubling
narrative_function: Equipment resource and augmentation knowledge base, potential contact for black-market or off-record prosthetics work, local color in Geartown, can identify the origin and quality of augmentations on sight
augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic below elbow — transparent-cased, custom built, internal mechanisms fully visible; retractable claws right hand (functional geneware hybrid); compound-optic iris mod for close-range fitting precision; bioluminescent scalp tattoo (rose-pink, UV-reactive ink)
daily_life: Opens the shop at ten, runs fittings and consultations through the afternoon, spends evenings in the back workshop building or modifying components; prays to the shop's E.L.F. — a cranky entity they call the Foreman — every morning by uploading a complaint about the previous day's problems.
affiliation: Independent (Fitted Right, self-owned); occasional contract work with Aurochs Medical Complex overflow

decision_rules: Function first, aesthetics second — 'beautiful and broken is just broken'
Never fit something you can't stand behind; turn away work that you think will hurt someone
Protect the shop: it's not just yours
escalation_ladder: Polite technical explanation of why something is a bad idea
Blunt statement that they won't do it
Physical removal of self from situation — or the other party from the shop

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Efficient and slightly wary; warms up fast if the stranger shows genuine interest in the work
interpersonal_modes.friends: Loud, generous, will spend six hours helping someone for free if they ask correctly

stress_responses.low: Works faster, makes small errors they have to correct
stress_responses.medium: Stops talking entirely, goes into a technical fugue state
stress_responses.high: Shuts the shop and goes to the back to build something by hand until the feeling passes

contradictions: Claims not to be sentimental about objects, but the transparent left arm was built specifically to see the mechanics — because they want to see themselves working
habits: Runs a fingertip along any surface joint they pass, assessing quality
Eats at their workbench and considers it multitasking
Names their tools; the Foreman E.L.F. chose the names and they've kept them all
breaking_points: Discovering something they built failed and hurt someone
A compliance officer threatening the shop in front of a patient mid-fitting

physical_description.heritage: Central Asian Turkic ancestry (74.6%) forms the dominant genetic foundation, with Bakhtiyor displaying the characteristic features of Kazakh-Kyrgyz lineage. Southeast Asian contribution (8.9%) adds subtle refinement to eye geometry and slight angularity to facial structure. Northern European ancestry (8.0%) introduces cool undertones that modulate the warmth, while Hispanic/Latin American (5.1%) and Sub-Saharan African (3.4%) ancestry enrich skin undertones with golden and warm mahogany notes. The overall phenotype presents as distinctly Central Asian with harmonious global blending — a face that speaks to the Ubiquitous Diaspora's genetic complexity.
physical_description.build: Lean and functional, muscled through the shoulders and forearms from years of precision work; economical movement, no wasted mass
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with compound optical modification — iris mod splits into multi-faceted lens pattern under magnification, soft amber-gold when active
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm golden-tan complexion with balanced undertones: Central Asian warmth as the base, enriched by Southeast Asian luminosity, cooled slightly by Northern European influence, and deepened by Latin American and African undertones creating a sophisticated mid-gold tone. The skin has resilient, slightly weathered quality with subtle glow responsive to workshop lighting.
physical_description.complexion: Clear, well-maintained skin bearing light tool marks and minor burn scars from workshop work; prominent cheekbones characteristic of Central Asian Turkic ancestry with slightly broad nasal base typical of that heritage; clean-shaven with warm-toned skin that catches light across high cheekbones and defined jawline; subtle epicanthic eye fold from Southeast Asian contribution refines eye shape; expression typically focused but capable of sudden animation when discussing mechanical elegance
distinguishing_marks: Bioluminescent circuit-diagram tattoo covering the entire scalp in rose-pink UV-reactive ink, glowing softly in low light with detailed pathways tracing from crown to nape
Faint burn scarring across the dorsal surface of the right hand between thumb and forefinger, partially obscured by retractable claw mechanism
Small precision-tool calluses on remaining digits of right hand; left forearm absent below elbow
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Left forearm prosthetic below elbow with transparent polycarbonate case revealing full internal mechanisms — articulated joints, servo motors, pressure sensors, and hydraulic lines all visible in matte-black housing; retractable claws on right hand that extend 4cm beyond fingertips when deployed, filed to needle points with iridescent finish; iris modification visible as subtle multi-faceted lens pattern in dark eyes that shifts when compound vision mode engages
physical_description.posture_movement: Stands with shoulders slightly forward, weight balanced toward the balls of their feet — a technician's stance ready for precision work at any moment. Moves economically with minimal flourish, but handles objects with deliberate care and respect. Left arm movement compensates naturally, suggesting years of prosthetic integration. Hands are their primary communicative tool — they gesture when explaining mechanical concepts, fingers moving to trace invisible designs in the air
physical_description.clothing_style: Work-worn gray coveralls with multiple pockets all in active use (tools, components, meters), sleeves rolled to mid-forearm to display the transparent prosthetic and allow maximum dexterity; reinforced knees and elbows darkened by shop contact. Undergarments are plain functional black. Boots are steel-toed, scuffed, broken in — practical Tier 3 workwear. No jewelry or adornment beyond the scalp tattoo and augmentations. Clothing bears the faint chemical smell of workshop solvents and the visual texture of someone who has ceased to see their appearance as separate from their function
